HELIOS PASTORAL HP Property Management Bagumbayan St., Naga 4400 Dear Mr. Pastoral: This has reference to the letters you sent to this Department which we consolidated as these all refer to one common query, seeking an opinion on the Decision rendered by Mr. Rolando D. Narvaez, the Zoning Administrator of the Municipality of Goa, Province of Camarines Sur. In your letter, you alleged that said Decision is violative of Goa Municipal Ordinance No. 195, Series of 2005 when "it combined two zones or districts and disregard the provisions of the interpretation of District Boundaries" as so indicated in the same municipal ordinance. The assailed Decision pértains to the denial by the Zoning Administrator of Mr. Pastoral's application for the issuance of a Locational Clearance for the proposed commercial building to be constructed on a portion on Lot 7 located at Rizal Street, Barangay Panday, Goa, Camarines Sur. Lot 7, according to Mr. Narvaez, is registered under the name of the Archdiocese of Nueva Caceres and was said to have been RECLASSIFIED as General Commercial Zone with Open Space/Park Portion. However, a scrutiny of Municipal Ordinance No. 195, Series of 2005, showed that Lot No. 7 is classified as a Residential/CommerciaI Lot. To support your claim, you submitted additional documents which showed that you have already filed an appeal on the Decision of Zoning Administrator Mr. Narvaez before the Local Zoning Board of Assessment and Appeals (LBZAA). As of date, said appeal is still pending before the said board. You also submitted to this Department Certification from the Office of the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan of Goa, Camarines Sur that the zoning ordinance, Municipal Ordinance No. 195, Series of 2005 has not been amended nor superseded. This Department's Opinion as rendered by the Legal Service: While there may be an appeal on the Decision of Zoning Administrator that is now pending before the LBZAA, the issue you raised for the Board's disposition was the alleged impropriety of combining two zones or districts, in utter disregard of the provisions of interpretation of District Boundaries. Thus, we shall no longer tackle this issue in deference to the LBZAA's jurisdiction.

However, considering that an issue on reclassification is apparent, we shall discuss the same for academic purposes. The Local Government Code grants to municipalities and cities the power to prescribe limits on the use of property, adopt comprehensive land use plans, enact zoning ordinances, and reclassify land within their jurisdictions. A city or municipality may, through an ordinance passed by the sanggunian after conducting public hearings for the purpose, authorize the reclassification of agricultural lands and provide for the manner of their utilization or disposition. (Section 20, RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Thus, a reclassification made without a requisite ordinance is deemed not valid. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, JES SECR LS:55/_ M.
